title: Tracing the first difference
goal: Find the first comparison that disagrees with the contract, then check the fix with neighbouring inputs.

prerequisites.text: Two-sided conditions, logical OR and separate stdout and stderr.

terms.title: Trace
terms.definition: Intermediate values or condition results recorded in execution order.

terms.title: First difference
terms.definition: The earliest observed fact that differs from the contract-based prediction.

sections.title: Predict before you run
paragraphs: A sensor accepts measurements from 20 through 70. At 70, both rejection conditions should be false. Write down the two expected flags, below 0 and above 0, before running the code.
The accepted or invalid message goes to stdout. The trace goes to stderr so it does not change the contract for programs that read stdout.

sections.title: Where 70 and 71 take different paths
paragraphs: The read_value helper reads a complete line and supplies a long after validating the number text. The main branch answers a separate question: is that number allowed?
steps: Supply 70. The comparison 70 < 20 gives 0, then 70 > 70 also gives 0.
Stderr shows value 70 below 0 above 0. The program prints accepted to stdout.
Check the prediction at 69 and 71. At 71, above is the first flag to change, and the result becomes invalid.

sections.title: Find the earliest changed value
paragraphs: If the code uses >=, the output at 70 incorrectly becomes invalid. The value 70 and below 0 still match the prediction. Look for the first unexpected 1: above 1.
Our fprintf provides the trace. It reports just the facts we chose to record. A separate compile exercise omits a right-hand operand. Execution does not start for that build.

sections.title: Transfer the method to a different scale
paragraphs: Practice uses the range 30–90. Predict the flags for 90, then locate the incorrect comparison. After the change, check 89, 90 and 91 to cover all three neighbouring cases.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Find the first comparison that disagrees with the contract, then check the fix with neighbouring inputs.

selfcheck.prompt: The observed trace for 70 shows below 0 and above 1. What differs first?
feedback: 70 is in range, so above should be 0.
70 is not below 20. The below 0 flag is expected.

selfcheck.prompt: Which one input reveals changing > 70 to >= 70?
What two predictions would you record for 90 in practice, and which line would reveal the fault?
selfcheck.feedback: Expect below 0 and above 0. With the fault, the trace reports value 90 below 0 above 1, although the result should be accepted.

practice.title: A measurement at 90
practice.task: The range 30–90 is inclusive. Read the first line as a decimal integer with an optional sign and surrounding whitespace. For numeric input, write two flags to stderr and accepted or invalid to stdout. For malformed input, write only invalid to stdout. Compare your prediction with the trace at 90 and repair one condition.
criteria: At 90, stdout is accepted and stderr contains value 90 below 0 above 0.
89 gives accepted; 91 and 29 give invalid. Confirm 30 as the valid lower boundary.
Explain the first difference using the above flag. Keep the trace and result formats unchanged.
practice.hint: Compare the expected and observed above flag at exactly 90. Reject only values higher than 90.

steps.action: Write the expected below and above flags for 90, then run the starter.
steps.expected: stdout: invalid. stderr: value 90 below 0 above 1.

steps.action: Fix the upper-bound comparison, then rerun 90.
steps.why: Retest the branch where the prediction and trace disagreed.
steps.expected: stdout: accepted. stderr: value 90 below 0 above 0.

steps.action: Run 89 and 91, then the lower-bound pair 29 and 30.
steps.why: Confirm behaviour on both sides of each boundary.
steps.expected: 89 and 30 are accepted. 91 and 29 are rejected.

exercises.title: Independent transfer
exercises.task: In a separate copy, use 40–60 and design a test for a faulty lower boundary.
criteria: 40 gives accepted; 39 gives invalid. The prediction identifies which comparison changes the below flag.
